Your data on universal access ignores how it prioritises bureaucracy over lives, while profit-driven alternatives with regulation actually save more by boosting efficiency.
Evidence from Germany's mixed model convinces me private input outperforms because it slashes waits and protects the vulnerable better than any well-funded state monopoly ever could.
Why cling to a system that kills through slowness when competition delivers faster, fairer results?
